title: Intent from Homebrew on Linux and macOS, with no source checkout: Linux binaries on every release
objective:
A developer installs Intent with Homebrew on Linux or macOS and has a working Intent with no checkout of Intent's source tree: the CLI, the daemon, the hooks and skills, and the pre-commit gate. Every release tag on GitHub carries Linux packages built by GitHub Actions beside the macOS assets, and the tap's formula installs the one that fits the machine. Windows is reached through WSL, which is ST0082's, built on this thread; there is no native Windows port.

Concretely:

1. A release workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, and packages them with the support payload the binaries read at run time, so a download installs rather than being a bare binary.
2. The binaries run on Linux distributions older than the build host: they are linked statically against musl, and the workflow proves it by running them in a container at an old floor.
3. A `workflow_dispatch` run builds the same packages without a tag, so a tag is never the workflow's first run.
4. The Linux packages reach each tag's GitHub release with one writer per release object, so nothing in CI races the local release flow's `gh release create`.
5. The formula in `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries Linux entries for both architectures beside the macOS one, written by the release tooling, so `brew install` works on Linux as it does on macOS.
6. Intent installed from its Linux package works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM, whose coreutils are uutils and whose awk is mawk.
7. The docs carry Intent's Linux install through Homebrew.
8. `intent daemon start --at-login` and `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuse on Linux before they write anything.
context:
Restructured on hv's word of 2026-10-14, in vc's session: "a new ST for both Intent and Devbin for both to run from a brew install on a Linux AND macOS install without the need for a local repo checkout of the source tree. THEN: we make ST0081 depend on that new ST." This thread opened on 2026-10-12 as Intent on Windows through WSL and already held that new thread's foundation: the Linux packages (WP-01), their place on each release (WP-02) and the `--at-login` refusal (WP-05), with work landed and tracked files naming ST0081 for it. So under vc's pen the numbers were swapped rather than the work moved: this thread became the Homebrew thread, and its WSL work became ST0082, which depends on it. The WSL page, half of the former WP-03, and the real Windows install, WP-04, went to ST0082 with their criteria AC-03.1, AC-03.2 and AC-04.1, which are descoped there, and so did the context that is only about WSL.

macOS stands as it is. hv, 2026-10-14: "No, not this mac. The macOS pipeline is fine. I have already tested it on a mac back home (gyges) and it all worked ok. We can loop back and retest later, but that route is ok and we don't need to worry about it for now." So hv's decision 17 holds: rhadamanth keeps the dev tree as the delivery, with brew installed, unlinked and pinned, and the aim of no source checkout is for every other machine.

In lock-step with Devbin, whose half is devbin#0195: a tap, `matthewsinclair/homebrew-devbin`, whose formula runs devbin's own installer from the release tag, and a release step that bumps it. Devbin is to carry its own thread for it (hv, 2026-10-14), with its WSL thread ST0008 depending on that thread as ST0082 depends on this one. devbin's formula needs only a pushed tag; Intent's needs the Linux packages on a release, so it waits on WP-02 and D55. devbin's joint check installs this thread's Linux package, so the package names go to devbin-vc as soon as they exist.

As built, measured 2026-10-12 on main a581c15c7 and on GitHub's v3.2.3:

- `rust.yml` builds and tests on Linux for every push to main that touches `native/rust`, `schema` or `surface`, and for pull requests, and adds macOS on tags and on `workflow_dispatch`. It uploads nothing.
- v3.2.3's release assets are macOS arm64 only (`intent-aarch64-apple-darwin`, `intentd-aarch64-apple-darwin`, `Intent.app.zip`, `intent-support.tar.gz`), all made outside CI by devbin's release flow.
- The binaries read their templates from an install root found from the executable's own location, so a bare binary is not an install. Whether `intent-support.tar.gz` serves Linux unchanged is WP-01's first measurement.
- The Linux build is already exercised by the Linux leg on every qualifying push. The risk this thread carries is packaging, release mechanics and where repos live, not compilation.
- `bin/devbin release check` warns on any workflow that has a `tags:` trigger and calls `gh release`, an upload included (`check_release_writers` in `bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/release`: one writer per release object). devbin is vendored here, so a change to its release steps is the Devbin project's to make.

Measured 2026-10-14 on main 72732afb4:

- `.github/workflows/linux-release.yml` (WP-01, landed at 86e4b0f7d) is dispatch-only and has not run, because nothing has been pushed since. It builds both musl triples, x86_64 on `ubuntu-latest` and aarch64 on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, through `bin/int linux` doctor, build, package and smoke, and smokes each package in `oraclelinux:7-slim` as the floor.
- The tap's formula for 3.2.3 declares `depends_on :macos` and arm64, by hv's ruling of 2026-08-15, so `brew install` refuses on Linux. This thread widens that ruling to Linux, on hv's word above.

Out of scope: a native Windows build, and apt.

Separate from this thread, and outside Intent's tree: the other estate mirrors GitHub's tags (v3.2.3 and later) and main to its own server from a bare clone of GitHub outside every Intent checkout, and each sync starts on vc's word that a release is tagged. hv ruled on 2026-10-12, through that estate's dc node, that its server also hosts each release's binaries beside the tag, starting with the first release that ships Linux binaries (3.2.4 if this thread lands in it), while v3.2.3 stays tag-only. Each sync copies the GitHub release's notes and files as they are, so the asset names and any checksum file this thread puts on GitHub's release are what that estate gets.

hv's rulings in vc's session, 2026-10-12, that stay with this thread: it rides Intent 3.2.4, built by cc after the 3.2.4 CHANGELOG section; WP-01's dispatch run goes first, because it produces the packages devbin's joint check installs; and `intent daemon start --at-login` refuses on Linux before it writes anything (WP-05). Still open for hv: how the packages reach the release (devbin's D55: devbin's release core attaches CI-built assets, which is devbin's proposal and the lean of both vcs, or an upload-only workflow here), and a checksum file on each release.

Linux proving, hv's rulings of 2026-10-12 given to devbin-vc and relayed: the tests run on hv's Ubuntu VM before anything is pushed, nothing goes to GitHub until it works there, and there is one release, 3.2.4, cut only once the work runs on main's HEAD, with no run of releases in quick succession. So WP-01's steps live in one script, `bin/int linux`, which the VM runs by hand and the dispatch workflow calls, and the dispatch run follows the VM's proof and hv's push. The VM is hv's arm64 Ubuntu on rhadamanth (Parallels, guest host `kovacs`, upgrading from 24.04 to 26.04.1 that day), reachable from rhadamanth with `prlctl exec` and `ssh kovacs`. It proves aarch64 Linux natively and x86_64 only through Rosetta or CI, and it does not prove WSL. The tree reaches it as a git bundle of main, because nothing is pushed. A build inside it loads rhadamanth like any other heavy run, so it goes through the census and START/END.

kovacs as measured 2026-10-14 by kovacs-sysadm, read-only: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS on aarch64; its coreutils are uutils 0.10.0 and its awk is mawk, while sed, grep and find are GNU; 2 CPUs, 3.3 GB of memory and a 3.8 GB swap file; `/tmp` is a 1.7 GB tmpfs, so a build there points TMPDIR at disk; no Rust, musl-gcc, shellcheck, xmllint or Homebrew yet. kovacs-sysadm, a Claude Code session on the VM, runs the VM side on instructions from intent-vc and devbin-vc (hv, 2026-10-14). The tree now reaches it over ssh from rhadamanth, read-only and pinned to the commit each instruction names, with a bundle through the VM's shared folder as the fallback. Whether CI's Linux runner has uutils or mawk is not measured, so kovacs is where they are proven.

wps.title: Linux release binaries built by GitHub Actions
wps.objective: A workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, statically or against an old glibc floor because the distributions they will run on are not known, packages them with the support payload the binaries read at run time, runs the packaged `intent --version` inside a container at that floor, and keeps each package as a workflow artifact. It runs on `workflow_dispatch`, so it is proven before any tag runs it. Its first measurement is whether `intent-support.tar.gz` serves Linux unchanged. aarch64 became required on 2026-10-14, because Homebrew on Linux is proven first on hv's aarch64 VM.
wps.body:
## Closed on AC-01.1 and AC-01.2 (cc, 2026-10-22)

Both criteria are satisfied from run 39854556183, hv's `--ref main` workflow_dispatch of 2026-10-22 at the release commit 2e0e9215d, conclusion success. The x86_64 and aarch64 musl packages were built, packaged with the support payload and kept as workflow artifacts, and each package's `intent --version` ran inside `oraclelinux:7-slim`, the floor the workflow names, reading `intent 3.2.5 (2e0e9215d67f67c665d1b8179a7888555551c8e7) dev`. The evidence is `refs/bank/cc/0081/evidence/run-39854556183.txt` (blob baec68a54b14).

The objective's first measurement, whether `intent-support.tar.gz` serves Linux unchanged, is answered yes. Every one of the 180 support files each package carries (`intent/plugins` and `lib/templates`) is byte-identical, exec bits included, to v3.2.5's `intent-support.tar.gz` (sha256 d0938ba5832f). The tarball's only extra is three empty directories git does not track, `lib/templates/eng`, `issues` and `prime`, which were on the release Mac's working copy and not in CI's clean checkout, and which no code names. The binaries are statically linked against musl, so no glibc floor applies to them, and the workflow is dispatch-only, so no tag ever triggers it.

wps.title: Linux assets on each tag's GitHub release, one writer per release object
wps.objective: Each release tag's GitHub release carries the Linux assets beside the macOS ones, with one writer per release object. `bin/devbin release check` warns on a workflow that has a `tags:` trigger and calls `gh release`, an upload included, so there are two candidate shapes: the local release flow downloads the workflow's artifacts and uploads them after it creates the release, which changes devbin and so is the Devbin project's to build; or a workflow with no `tags:` trigger, dispatched once the release exists, uploads to it and never creates one. The chosen shape is written into `intent/docs/releasing.md`, and `bin/devbin release check` names no second writer.

wps.title: Intent's Linux install through Homebrew, in docs/install.md
wps.objective: `docs/install.md` carries Intent's Linux install in a bare `## Linux` section, so its anchor is `#linux`: Homebrew on Linux, then `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent`, `intent bootstrap` and `intent doctor`, with no checkout of Intent's source tree. It is the install step's one home: ST0082's WSL page links to it and never restates it, and devbin's README points at it. The page's sections on verifying an install and on what an install has to contain read true for the Linux package, by a line or by a pointer. Every command on the page is run on Linux before it is written down: drafted from hv's Ubuntu VM, and run again from the tap once a release carries the Linux packages. Whether devbin also installs Intent is the Devbin project's call; this install is needed either way. The WSL page this package also held moved to ST0082 on 2026-10-14. Its bank also carries this thread's two lines in the release's CHANGELOG section, one for the Linux packages and the Homebrew install on Linux and one for WP-05's `--at-login` refusal (vc under hv's pen, 2026-10-13, carried here 2026-10-14).

wps.title: First install on a real Windows machine
wps.status_reason: Moved to ST0082 as its WP-02 on hv's ruling of 2026-10-14: ST0081 became the Homebrew thread and its WSL work became ST0082, which depends on it. AC-04.1 is descoped to ST0082.
wps.objective: A developer installs Intent from a tagged release under WSL on a real Windows machine by following the docs, and reports `intent --version`, `intent doctor`, and one thread created and listed in a project in the WSL filesystem. hv arranges the run through the other estate; Intent's nodes cannot run it.

wps.title: intent daemon start --at-login refuses on Linux before writing anything
wps.objective: On a machine without launchd, `intent daemon start --at-login` refuses before it writes anything, so no `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` plist appears on Linux, and its remedy names `intent daemon start` without the flag as the way to run the daemon. `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuses the same way. Today `daemon_start` in `intent-cli/src/render.rs` writes the plist through `launchagent::write_plist` and only then fails at `launchctl`, whose `NoLaunchctl` remedy in `intentsvcs/src/launchagent.rs` already says the right thing; the refusal moves ahead of the write. Linux CI runs the test that proves it.

wps.title: The Homebrew formula installs Intent on Linux
wps.objective: The formula the release tooling writes for `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries Linux entries for x86_64 and aarch64 beside the macOS one, each pointing at that release's Linux package, so `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent` works on Linux with no source checkout, as it does on macOS. The 3.2.3 formula declares `depends_on :macos` and arm64, by hv's ruling of 2026-08-15, which hv widened to Linux on 2026-10-14. Until a release carries Linux packages, the formula is rehearsed on hv's Ubuntu VM from a local copy against the package the VM built. The install from the tap is proven once the first release with Linux packages is published, and the macOS install is re-proven on a Mac with no checkout when hv loops back to it. Shape agreed on 2026-10-14 (cc's proposal, vc's yes under hv's pen): the formula writer, and smoke beside it, move out of `cmd/macos` to one home both release steps call. `on_linux` entries for each architecture override the top-level url, which stays macOS arm64's because `brew tap` validates every simulated platform. `depends_on :macos` goes, and `arch: :arm64` moves inside `on_macos` with the intentd and support resources. The Linux branch installs the unpacked package into libexec and shares the chmod and symlink tail. Every sha256 is read from the bytes the release serves. A dev-tap input of base URL plus hashes lets hv's Ubuntu VM prove the formula from file:// URLs before any push. publish asks for its own assets by name instead of refusing any release that already carries assets, and its notes stop saying macOS-only.
wps.body:
## Closed on AC-06.1 (vc's ruling (a) under hv's pen, 2026-10-22)

The work package's one criterion, AC-06.1, is satisfied (6a5d06b5d) from kovacs ORDER 8. On aarch64 Linux with no Intent and no checkout of Intent's source, `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent` from the published tap at 1de8ca7e5 installed v3.2.5's aarch64 Linux package, the formula's `on_linux` `on_arm` entry (sha256 3ccb521acc97, which vc verified against the release's assets and brew checks on download), and the installed `intent --version` read `intent 3.2.5 (2e0e9215d67f67c665d1b8179a7888555551c8e7) release`. The run's lines are `refs/bank/cc/0081/evidence/o8-postcut-lines.txt` (blob b3fc943efce9).

The formula that run installed has the shape the objective describes, as read from the tap at 1de8ca7e5: the top-level url stays macOS arm64's, `on_macos` carries `depends_on arch: :arm64` with the intentd and support resources, `depends_on :macos` is gone, and `on_linux` has `on_intel` and `on_arm` entries pointing at the release's x86_64 and aarch64 musl packages.

The objective's macOS clause, that the macOS install is re-proven on a Mac with no checkout when hv loops back to it, is conditional on hv, and no criterion carries it. The clean-Mac install has been proven once, on gyges at 3.2.0 on 2026-09-21: ST0056's AC-00.5 and AC-11.1 are satisfied from `intent/st/ST0056/gyges-install.md`. A re-proof at 3.2.5 is hv's loop-back, carried in `intent/wip.md`'s TODO.

wps.title: Intent on Ubuntu from its Linux package, as a user uses it
wps.objective: Intent installed from its Linux package, with no checkout of Intent's source, works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM, whose coreutils are uutils and whose awk is mawk. The drive covers `intent --version` and `intent bootstrap`; a new project in which `intent doctor` reports no finding; the thread, work package and acceptance verbs; the whiteboard; the daemon started and stopped without `--at-login`, and the `--at-login` refusal; `intent claude upgrade --apply`, with its hooks firing in a Claude Code session; and the critic gate with shellcheck on PATH. Intent's shell suite runs once on the same host, because uutils and mawk are what Ubuntu 26.04 ships. Every step runs as a bash script with its log, never as commands typed into an agent's own shell, whose `grep` and `find` are wrappers. Each defect found is filed as an issue and fixed before the push, and the drive runs again on the commit that is pushed.
wps.body:
## The package drive (ORDER 7b)

`o7-drive-b.sh` (blob 3e1d3738a8ba, sha256 e5080df8...3481) ran on kovacs, hv's Ubuntu VM, by hv's own `!` in kovacs-sysadm's session on 2026-10-16 from 20:18:26Z to 20:18:27Z, against ORDER 3's package (sha256 f289e5f1...d28d). It passed at rc 0 with all 32 steps as wanted. The host has 2 CPUs on aarch64, kernel 7.0.0-38, uutils coreutils date 0.10.0 and mawk 1.3.4 20260129, with git, jq, tar and shellcheck present.

- `intent --version`, `info`, `bootstrap` and `bootstrap --check`; `init`; `intent doctor` reported "0 finding(s)".
- `st`, `wp` and `ac` new and list; `ac gate` answered rc 1, BLOCKED, as wanted.
- `wb register`, `pickup`, `add` and `show`.
- `daemon start`, `status` and `stop`; `--at-login` start and stop each refused at rc 1 with no LaunchAgents written.
- `claude upgrade --apply` wired the git hooks and the settings. The hooks: SessionStart 0; a prompt blocked at rc 2 with `Expected sentinel:`; a prompt released at 0; Stop 0.
- A clean commit landed as 3bc1898; a commit was refused at rc 1 on CRITICAL IN-SH-CODE-001 at `bad.sh:4`. The critic said "shell -- 4 rule(s) could not be armed at all: 4 declared unanswerable" and "2 of 6 rule(s) ASKED of this run".
- `intent doctor` at the end: 0 findings, 1 advisory not counted.

The log is `~/work/intent-vc/o7-drive.log` on kovacs, 10666 bytes, sha256 2beb559f...7102. With hv's real Claude Code session on kovacs, the evidence decision 63 satisfied AC-07.1 on, this drive is the work package's remaining half. The clean install from the published tap is AC-06.1's and comes after the cut.

Each package is kept as a workflow artifact: intent-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl (artifact 12459447395, 14576654 bytes, digest sha256:9c386af2b961) and intent-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl (artifact 12459690768, 13589688 bytes, digest sha256:e63d2e01e4cc), both kept until 2027-01-20. criteria.text: The same run executes the packaged `intent --version` inside a container of the oldest Linux distribution the workflow names as its floor, and that step fails the run when the binary does not start.

state.evidence: The same run, 39854556183 (hv's --ref main workflow_dispatch of 2026-10-22, conclusion success). In both jobs (ids 120089246768 and 120089247186) the step `smoke, on the floor (AC-01.2)` ran `bin/int linux smoke --in "$FLOOR"` with FLOOR oraclelinux:7-slim, the one floor the workflow names (Oracle Linux 7, glibc 2.17), pulled at digest sha256:1add6ed8602e. Inside that container the packaged binary, reached through a link on PATH, printed `intent 3.2.5 (2e0e9215d67f67c665d1b8179a7888555551c8e7) dev` on each leg, then resolved its install root to /opt/intent-<triple> and ran the support tree's gate hook both ways. The step fails the run when the binary does not start, by reading: bin/.devbin/cmd/linux runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 20) and pipes smoke_checks into the container's `/bin/bash -euo pipefail -s`, whose first check is `intent --version`, so a binary that does not start ends the container's shell non-zero, which ends `bin/int` non-zero, which fails the step (its shell, as the log shows, is `/usr/bin/bash -e {0}`), the job and the run; that clause was read, not driven with a broken binary. Both floor steps are quoted in refs/bank/cc/0081/evidence/run-39854556183.txt (blob baec68a54b14).
